name: Ergothioneine

card.summary: A mushroom-derived antioxidant amino acid studied for skin protection and healthy ageing and sold as a supplement and skincare ingredient.

quick.overview:
Ergothioneine is a sulfur-containing amino acid made by fungi and bacteria; humans obtain it from foods such as mushrooms. It is taken or applied as an antioxidant for skin and ageing.

Reviews describe antioxidant and cytoprotective activity and a dedicated transporter in the body, and a review of its skin pathways exists; clinical trials focus mainly on other outcomes.
quick.how: Eaten via mushrooms or supplements, or applied in skincare serums.
quick.risks: The European Food Safety Authority set safe intake levels, and reviews describe it as regulatory-approved as safe.

lead: Ergothioneine is a naturally occurring amino acid, first isolated from ergot fungus by Charles Tanret in 1909.[1] Humans get it only from diet; mushrooms are the richest source.[1][2]

A review describes potent antioxidant activity and a dedicated transporter, SLC22A4.[2][3] A 2023 review examined its mechanisms in skin.[4] People use it for skin protection and as an anti-ageing ingredient.

angle.text: Used in serums and supplements for antioxidant protection of skin. Evidence is largely mechanistic.

paras: A pilot randomised trial examined ergothioneine for cognitive decline in mildly impaired subjects.[5] Reviews summarise antioxidant mechanisms.[3] No trial on cosmetic skin outcomes was identified; a review covers skin mechanisms.[4]
